module_docs: Java writes the kick message with `NetworkBuffer.JSON_COMPONENT`
component to JSON, and that JSON text goes out as a `STRING`; reading
parses the string and decodes it back. The port does the same through
Key-order note: the JSON text comes from `serde_json::Value::to_string`,
whose object keys sort lexicographically, while Java's Gson preserves the
writer's insertion order. The two agree whenever the writer emits keys in
sorted order — plain-text and single-key shapes, including the recorded
fixture below. A styled component's key order may differ textually from
Java's while decoding to the same tree.
